title: County of Pallars Sobirà
capsule: The County of Pallars Sobirà (upper Pallars) was a Pyrenean county in the upper valley of the Noguera Pallaresa, in what is now Lleida province, Catalonia. It originated from the partition of the older County of Pallars between the sons of Count Sunyer, with the upper portion crystallising as a distinct comital domain by the mid-11th century under counts such as Artau I (r. c. 1049–1081), whose nobles offset the region's meagre mountain resources through raiding and shifting alliances with neighbouring counties. Through the 12th century the county passed among the Houses of Pallars, Comminges, and Mataplana while remaining a small, autonomous Pyrenean lordship.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's history is documented in Catalan chronicles and comital charters, but the precise western and northern limits in the high Pyrenees were contested and are reconstructed from ecclesiastical rather than political boundary records.
